headline: Garage Conversion vs Home Addition: How to Choose for Your Household
articleBody:
When you need extra room for an aging parent, home office, or growing family, deciding between converting an attached garage and building a brand-new room addition comes down to cost, yard space, and layout goals.

Key differences
A garage conversion uses your existing roofline, foundation, and exterior walls, which usually keeps construction simpler than pouring a new foundation from scratch. However, converting means losing covered vehicle parking and storage space. An exterior home addition preserves your garage completely and allows you to design custom square footage anywhere on the lot, but it involves ground excavation, new foundation footings, and tying into existing roofing.

Cost and timeline tradeoffs
Garage conversions typically take less time because the main structure already stands. You still have to budget for leveling the concrete slab, adding wall and ceiling insulation, running dedicated HVAC ducts or mini-splits, and pulling structural and electrical permits. An addition requires full site preparation, framing, and roofing, resulting in a larger overall investment and a longer construction timeline.

How to Compare Your Options
If your lot has strict setback lines or limited yard space, a garage conversion is often the most practical choice. If keeping your cars protected from Florida weather is non-negotiable, an addition makes better sense.
